figure: the realistic mantle card on the closed 2-D annulus, QuaST (top) vs ASPECT (bottom)

card.geometry: PolarAnnulus(R0=1.22, R1=2.22, Phi=2*pi; seam=:periodic); gap d = 1 is the physics length unit, d = 2.9e6 m (ASPECT)
card.boundaries: free slip on both circles, T = 1 (1500 K) inner, T = 0 (500 K) outer, remove net rotation (ASPECT)
card.physics: H = 10, Boussinesq, nominal Ra = 1e5 at the composite calibration point; composite isostress diffusion+dislocation rheology (A_d=1.6240183119e5, A_s=2.6796419238e-1, E_d=12, E_s=17, n=3, eta_T0=0.5, eps_min=1e-12, eta_min=1e-4, eta_max=1e4), two phase transitions z0 = 0.87 (+0.032, B=1.8182) and z0 = 0.78 (-0.032, B=3.0303) with per-phase latent heat (L=0.11), no yielding/weakening
card.initial_condition: 0.05 sin(pi h) cos(2 phi) + 0.02 sin(2 pi h) cos(4 phi) on top of the annular H-inclusive conductive base, h=(r-R0)/d, phi=atan2(y,x)

measured.note: not recorded: the 30k arm was stopped before the run's final summary line; the plates and the per-frame diagnostics come from the saved frames (eta_interior_node is in the frame meta)

card.amr_quast: AMR: balanced every=5 steps refine_frac=0.2 coarsen_frac=0.05 max_leaves=30000 max_level=7 wall_min_level=5 wall_strip=0.1 hysteresis=1 gate=true symmetry=none indicator=theta initial_refine=0

no_nusselt: The per-wall Nusselt pair is undefined on this card by design (H = 10 makes the H-inclusive base conductive flux negative at the inner circle, -dTbar/dr(R0) = -4.3058), so the QuaST arm runs nu_undefined=:nan and the frame stream has no Nusselt column.  The figure therefore shows V_rms / mean T / T_max instead of a Nusselt pair; this is a deliberate property of the card, not missing data.

conversions.velocity: u_nd = u * d / kappa, d/kappa = 2.9e12 s
conversions.viscosity: eta_nd = eta / eta0, eta0 = 2.368635e23 Pa s
conversions.time: t_nd = t * kappa / d^2 = t / 8.41e18 s

quast.field_eta: frame_%05d_eta.bin, the solver's own nodal log10(eta/eta_ref)

aspect.field_eta: the saved nodal `viscosity`, converted with eta_nd = eta/eta0 (the realistic composite plugin clamps it to the card's [eta_min, eta_max], so it is usable; cross-checked against the card's composite law in --check)

layout.supersampling: master rendered at 4x the 1200 px canvas and Lanczos-downsampled to 1200 px for the GIF, poster and the 1200 px mp4
layout.header: none: nothing above the panels, no title and no per-frame time text; the card and the frame provenance are in this sidecar and the README caption
layout.row_labels: QuaST / ASPECT inside the temperature panels, bold white Computer Modern with a thin dark outline
layout.plates: lower-right 60 % white plates: V_rms / mean T / T_max; theta min/max; log10 eta min/max; leaves-or-cells / level range

theta_definition.grid: common polar grid of 800 radial x 4096 angular cell centres (3276800 points), identical for both codes
theta_definition.note: <T>_phi(r) is the angular mean at each radius on the common grid: a diagnostic of the state, not a solver variable; the annular analogue of the box clip's horizontal-mean anomaly

rasterisation.method: exact Q2 tensor-basis evaluation on each code's own leaves: the leaves of one tree level tile a dyadic lattice in logical (S, T) coordinates, so each level is evaluated in one vectorised pass and painted coarse->fine; the finest cell containing each polar-grid point wins
rasterisation.quast: frame_%05d_mesh.csv leaves (logical S,T) + the solver's Q2 node cloud; each leaf's nine Q2 nodes are looked up in the node cloud (max distance < 1e-9) and the Q2 basis is evaluated exactly
rasterisation.aspect: each VTU parent cell is the group of four linear sub-quads on nine consecutive Q2 nodes; the level is inferred from the cell area and mid radius, and the nine node values are evaluated with the Q2 tensor basis on the cell's dyadic polar rectangle
rasterisation.mesh_panel: level/cell-id raster on the panel's own pixel grid (one white boundary pixel at the 2x master, i.e. the reference's white 0.42 pt cell outlines)

mesh_boundaries.policy: every cell's boundary is drawn in white while the cell is at least 0.67 delivered (1200 px canvas) pixels across, at the reference's ~0.5 delivered px outline weight (scale-independent); below that a cell is colour-filled and only the level-boundary contours are drawn (a level-7 ASPECT cell of this card is ~0.5 px across at 279 px, so outlining all ~160 000 of them would fill the mesh panel white)
mesh_boundaries.note: the per-row list is the drawable flag of each level, coarsest first; the level legend is shared by both rows

mesh_definition.quast: per-frame leaves of QuaST's balanced tree, coloured by tree level; the coarse ring is 8 radial x 80 angular at level 3
mesh_definition.aspect: per-frame active cells, coloured by the tree level inferred from the cell area; the coarse shell is 12 x 1, the card's Initial global refinement = 5 (level 5)
mesh_definition.level_calibration: a tree level is each code's own: on this card QuaST's levels 5-7 are (320x32, 640x64, 1280x128) leaves and ASPECT's 5-7 are (384x32, 768x64, 1536x128) cells, i.e. the same refinement scale within ~20 % in the range the figure shows; the level numbers are not frozen against each other

log10_eta.norm: power law (box-clip mapping): colour = ((log10 eta - vmin)/(vmax - vmin))**0.30; the bar labels the true log10 values, dark = stiff = cold

level.colours: discrete, one colour per tree level

eta_definition.quantity: log10(eta/eta_ref) with eta_ref = 1 (nondimensional) = eta0 = 2.368635e23 Pa s
eta_definition.quast: the solver's composite-isostress nodal field written per frame (frame_%05d_eta.bin)
eta_definition.aspect: the saved nodal `viscosity` of ASPECT's realistic composite material model (ASPECT's diffusion-dislocation partition with the card's prefactors), eta_nd = eta/eta0; the plugin clamps it to [eta_min, eta_max] of the card
eta_definition.note: each row shows the material state its own solver used; the two laws are the same isostress diffusion+dislocation family calibrated at the same card point, not a fitted reproduction

matching.rule: one target list in time; each row shows the nearest available frame (no time interpolation), the offset delta = t_frame - t_target is recorded per target
matching.quast_frame_cadence: one frame every 5 steps plus one step past every AMR cycle (and the final state)

caption: The realistic mantle card (H = 10, nominal Ra = 1e5 at the composite calibration point) on the closed 2-D annulus, run by QuaST (top) and by ASPECT (bottom) from the same analytic initial state, each on its own adaptive mesh, over the dynamically active phase t_nd = 1e-6 to 1.2e-4: total temperature, its anomaly about the angular mean at each radius, log10(eta/eta_ref) of the composite isostress rheology on the power-law colour mapping (gamma = 0.30, bar labels the true range, dark = stiff = cold), and each code's own adaptive mesh coloured by tree level. Both rows share one colour scale per column. The card has no Nusselt pair by design (H = 10 makes the per-wall normalisation undefined), so the temperature plate carries V_rms, mean T and T_max instead. QuaST runs its balanced AMR with a 30,000-leaf budget; its 30k arm was stopped at t_nd = 1.243e-4 because at the full leaf budget the direct solve slowed to about two minutes per step and the 26 GB WSL memory of the development machine began to swap, so the clip ends at the end of the plume-growth phase; the earlier full-window clip (t_nd = 1e-6 .. 3.2e-4) used a 10,000-leaf budget. No header or card text is drawn: the card, the measured numbers and the provenance are in the JSON sidecar and in this caption.
notes: The two mesh panels compare two independent adaptive discretizations: QuaST's gradient-jump indicator with a wall minimum level vs ASPECT's temperature strategy (20 % refine / 0.5 % coarsen); the cell counts and level ranges are each code's own and are printed on the plates.
Each row shows its own nearest frame in time (the offset delta is recorded per target in `matching.targets`); there is no time interpolation, only spatial rasterisation.

Mesh-panel boundary policy: every cell outline is drawn while the cell is at least 0.67 delivered px across; a level-7 ASPECT cell of this card is ~0.5 px across at 279 px, so for such sub-pixel levels the panel is colour-filled with the level-contour outlines only (outlining all ~160 000 cells at the delivered size would fill the panel white).  Pass --mesh-min-cell-px 0.3 to draw every outline instead.
This is a demonstration of the same-card comparison, not an accuracy claim: the two codes advance the transient with different integrators and time-step sequences.
The ASPECT row's viscosity is the saved material field, not a reconstruction; --check cross-checks it against the card's composite law with the Q2 strain rate and reports the difference.

QuaST row: 30,000-leaf budget, stopped at step 850 / t_nd = 1.24345e-4 because at the full leaf budget the direct solve fell to about two minutes per step and the 26 GB WSL memory began to swap; the tracked clip therefore covers t_nd = 1e-6 .. 1.2e-4.  The earlier 10,000-leaf run covered the full 1e-6 .. 3.2e-4 window.

Renderer options used for this revision: 4x master supersampling, 800 x 4096 polar sampling, 2x mesh supersampling, font scale 1.25 (two-line T plate) and 75 % white plates, GIF with --gif-dither none.

quast_run.note: the 30k arm was stopped at step 850 (t_nd = 1.24345e-4) because at the full 30k leaf budget the direct solve took about two minutes per step and the development machine's 26 GB WSL memory began to swap; frames and a checkpoint (step 800) are kept in out_julia/annulus_realistic/quast_prod30*
